definition: Figurative language is the use of a word or phrase in a meaning different from its usual one, especially when a vivid sensory image is used to express an abstract idea or relation. In this historical source, its aesthetic effect comes from the feeling stirred by the image, the associations it brings, and the perceived analogy linking unlike things.
